description: A time-in-force bucket's count is the number of joined risk/margin records, so orders with several risk/margin records count once per record.

b.request: Join risk/margin records to their orders on `riskandmargin.ordervault` = `orders.recordvault` (inner join, dropping records with no matching order), count joined risk/margin records per `orders.timespan` value (so an order with several risk/margin records counts once per record, and NULL time-in-force is its own bucket), compute each bucket's share of the summed bucket counts, keep buckets whose share is above the average share across buckets, and return one row with the total count of those kept buckets, their average share, and their average excess over the overall average share, all unrounded
b.sql: WITH b AS (SELECT o.timespan, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM riskandmargin r JOIN orders o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.timespan), s AS (SELECT timespan, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM b), a AS (SELECT timespan, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT COUNT(*) AS kept_buckets, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess FROM a WHERE share > avg_share

a.request: Match risk/margin records to their orders (`riskandmargin.ordervault` = `orders.recordvault`) and leave out risk/margin records with no matching order. Group the matched pairs by time in force (`orders.timespan`); orders with no time in force form their own bucket. Give each bucket a count equal to the number of matched risk/margin records in it, so an order with two risk/margin records adds 2. Each bucket's share is its count divided by the total of all bucket counts. Keep only the buckets whose share is above the plain average of all the bucket shares. Return one summary row with three values: the total count across the kept buckets, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds that average share. Don't round anything.
a.sql: WITH b AS (SELECT o.timespan AS ts, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM riskandmargin r JOIN orders o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.timespan), s AS (SELECT ts, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM b), a AS (SELECT ts, cnt, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s), k AS (SELECT * FROM a WHERE share > avg_share) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess FROM k

c.request: Take risk/margin records matched to their orders (`riskandmargin.ordervault` = `orders.recordvault`), skipping any with no matching order, and get each time-in-force (`orders.timespan`) bucket's count. Orders with no time in force are their own bucket. Work out each bucket's share of the total of all bucket counts, and keep the buckets whose share is above the average share. Give me one summary row with three values: the total count across those buckets, their average share, and how far above the average share they are on average. Leave everything unrounded. A time-in-force bucket's count is the number of joined risk/margin records, so orders with several risk/margin records count once per record.
c.sql: WITH b AS (SELECT o.timespan, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM riskandmargin r JOIN orders o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.timespan), s AS (SELECT timespan, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM b), a AS (SELECT timespan, cnt, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_avg_share FROM a WHERE share > avg_share

d.request: Take risk/margin records matched to their orders (`riskandmargin.ordervault` = `orders.recordvault`), skipping any with no matching order, and count the joined risk/margin records in each time-in-force (`orders.timespan`) bucket, so an order with several risk/margin records counts once per record. Orders with no time in force form their own bucket. Work out each bucket's share of the total of all bucket counts, and keep the buckets whose share is above the average share. Give me one summary row with three values: the total count across those buckets, their average share, and how far above the average share they are on average. Leave everything unrounded.
d.sql: WITH buckets AS (SELECT o.timespan AS tif, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM riskandmargin r JOIN orders o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.timespan), shares AS (SELECT tif, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM buckets), avg_s AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares), kept AS (SELECT s.cnt, s.share, a.avg_share FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_s a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_avg_share FROM kept
